statement: CLI crate disables autobins and defines two binaries, ebound (src/main.rs) and entrybound (src/bin/entrybound.rs), plus library entrybound_cli.
decision_needed: Is the dual binary name (ebound plus entrybound alias) the frozen distribution naming?

statement: Both executables are thin wrappers calling entrybound_cli::main_entry; the alias test asserts byte-identical --help output for ebound and entrybound.
CLI pins exact dependency versions: entrybound path dep, rpassword =7.4.0, zeroize =1.9.0 (alloc); dev-deps bzip2 =0.6.1, crc32fast =1.5.0, flate2 =1.1.9, lzma-rust2 =0.20.0, zstd =0.13.3.
research_needed: Audit longevity/maintenance and supply-chain risk of pinned crates (rpassword, zeroize) and their MSRV compatibility.

statement: CLI inherits workspace package metadata: version 0.1.0, edition 2024, rust-version 1.94 (root Cargo.toml L5-8); lints inherited from workspace.
research_needed: Confirm MSRV 1.94 is acceptable for target distribution channels (distro packagers).
decision_needed: What MSRV and version scheme will the first stable CLI release use?

statement: main_entry maps diagnostic OutcomeClass to process exit codes: Ok 0, Unsupported 2, Truncated 3, Corrupt 4, Nonconforming 5, PolicyRefused 6; the Display form of the diagnostic is printed to stderr.
evidence_in_source: code; cli_workflow.rs:246-275 asserts exit 3 for truncated STREAM
decision_needed: Are these exit codes a frozen public contract, and should exit 1 remain unused?

statement: Usage errors (EB_CLI_USAGE) and I/O failures (EB_IO) both use OutcomeClass PolicyRefused and so share exit code 6; scripts cannot distinguish bad invocation from filesystem failure or policy refusal by exit status.
research_needed: Usability study of scripting against exit codes; compare tar/zip/7z exit conventions.
decision_needed: Should usage errors and I/O errors get distinct exit codes?

statement: A malformed archive yields a stable diagnostic line containing 'NONCONFORMING EB_ECF_BAD_MAGIC' on stderr and never a Rust Debug dump.
Top-level dispatch recognises help/--help/-h plus 14 commands: pack, convert, publish, sidecar, unpack, read, list, repack, diff, inspect, verify, sign, key, explain.
research_needed: CLI usability study of the 14-command surface versus incumbents (tar, zip, 7z).
decision_needed: Is the 14-command set the v1 CLI surface?

statement: Any unrecognised command fails with Unsupported EB_CLI_NOT_IMPLEMENTED ('command is not implemented'); the unit test uses 'salvage' as an example future command, so salvage/repair is not implemented.
research_needed: Define salvage/repair semantics and corruption-localization experiments.
decision_needed: Will salvage/repair ship in v1 or be deferred?

statement: Invoking with no command prints the global HELP and succeeds; 'help' with extra arguments is a usage error (ensure_no_more, L4913-4918).
The CLI self-identifies as 'Entrybound (experimental native bootstrap)', i.e. the entire command set is presented as experimental, not a stable release.
research_needed: Define exit criteria (conformance corpus, security review, format freeze) for dropping the experimental label.
decision_needed: What must be true before the CLI drops the 'experimental bootstrap' label?

statement: Help claims unencrypted Complete archives with directories, regular files, normalized CDC, archive-wide exact dedup, per-unique-Chunk STORE/Zstandard/LZ4/LZMA2 planning, reversible structural transforms, verified DEFLATE reconstruction, opportunistic JPEG/JPEG XL reconstruction, optional shared dictionaries and bounded ChunkGroups in dense/extreme.
evidence_in_source: help text; no measurement in slice
research_needed: Benchmark corpus showing each advertised technique is actually selected and beneficial per profile.

statement: Help says the build supports 'directories, regular files', yet list/inspect handle EntryKind Symlink and ReparsePoint (L3198-3203) and unpack has symlink/reparse policies; the capability text appears stale or narrower than the implementation.
decision_needed: Should help text enumerate symlinks and reparse points as supported entry kinds?

statement: Both layouts encode the same archive model and produce identical LAI, PCR and AUX, differing only in PCI, physical organisation and access capability.
evidence_in_source: help text; exercised indirectly by repack representation-only equality checks
research_needed: Property test across corpus: pack INDEXED vs STREAM and assert LAI/PCR/AUX equality, PCI difference.

statement: STREAM writes and reads without seeking, carries no Index, and cannot resolve one entry without a full sequential pass.

Crypto v1: metadata-private encrypted INDEXED archives using one or more X-Wing draft-10 hybrid recipients or one password-only Argon2id recipient; Ed25519 signatures detached or embedded as encrypted private CONTROL data; RFC 3161 verification offline against caller trust anchors.
research_needed: External security review; track X-Wing draft finalisation.

statement: Recipient KEM is pinned to 'X-Wing draft-10'; a pre-standard draft is frozen into crypto v1 user-facing semantics.
research_needed: Monitor IETF X-Wing/hybrid KEM standardisation; assess wire-compat impact of final RFC changes.
decision_needed: Will v1 ship on X-Wing draft-10 or wait for/migrate to the final specification?

statement: Help asserts encrypted INDEXED archives are 'metadata-private'.
research_needed: Leakage analysis of public framing (recipient count, stanza types, padding class, segment count, total bytes) printed by inspect --crypto.

statement: Authenticated recipient addition preserves the AFK; recipient removal and password rotation use full fresh-key re-encryption.
evidence_in_source: help text; commands at L2733-2838; crypto_cli.rs:184-260

statement: Encrypted STREAM is unsupported (help statement).
research_needed: Design/security analysis of an encrypted sequential layout.
decision_needed: Is encrypted STREAM deferred past v1 or a non-goal?

statement: '-' denotes standard input or output; whenever archive bytes go to stdout, all status output is routed to stderr (Status.to_stderr, L341-354).
evidence_in_source: code; test a_real_pipe_carries_a_stream_archive_from_pack_to_verify (cli_workflow.rs:117-157) asserts stdout carries only archive bytes

statement: Default creation profile is balanced; decoding is self-describing and never requires a profile.
evidence_in_source: code (profile.unwrap_or_default at L701; CompressionProfile default Balanced planner.rs:65-71); test pack_help_and_profile_option_are_available_only_at_creation (cli_workflow.rs:74-92) shows verify --profile is EB_CLI_USAGE

statement: Integration test pins observable identifiers: format 'ecf/bootstrap-v1', planner 'balanced-v6', chunker prefix 'gear-norm-v1/', codec ids 'store/v1' and 'zstandard/v1', whole-object reconstruction feature=true, index 'present and valid'.
decision_needed: Will the 'bootstrap-v1' format namespace be renamed before a stable format freeze?

statement: Test pins the ECF magic bytes 8E 'E' 'B' '1' 0D 0A 1A 0A and preamble byte 72 == 2 meaning STREAM layout.
CLI detects encrypted archives by reading 24 preamble bytes: magic match and FEATURE_ENCRYPTED_INDEXED_V1 bit in big-endian u64 at bytes 16..24; encryption presence is therefore publicly visible.
research_needed: Confirm that visible encrypted-feature bit is an accepted non-goal of metadata privacy.

statement: Reader selection uses the archive's declared layout (peek_layout over first 256 bytes), not source seekability; a header too short or damaged to classify falls back to the INDEXED random-access reader which owns the stable diagnostic.

load(): stdin always uses the sequential STREAM reader with bootstrap_sequential_limits and a caller content policy; a path declared STREAM uses the sequential reader over the file; other paths are read fully into memory and opened with ecf::open.
research_needed: Measure peak RSS of INDEXED open for large archives (whole-file read).

statement: Unencrypted INDEXED archives cannot be consumed from stdin by list/inspect/verify/explain/unpack: stdin is routed to the STREAM scanner, which refuses INDEXED with EB_ECF_UNSUPPORTED_REQUIRED_FEATURE (ecf/stream.rs:1147-1153), although pack can emit INDEXED to stdout with --layout indexed.
evidence_in_source: code path inference (L525-531, L2379-2386, L4788-4791) plus core stream.rs:1147-1153
research_needed: Decide whether buffered INDEXED-from-pipe support is needed; test pack --layout indexed - | verify -.
decision_needed: Should '-' input accept INDEXED archives by buffering, or should pack refuse --layout indexed to stdout?

statement: CLI-wide default limits come from bootstrap_resource_policy (entries 1,000,000; total logical 64 GiB; max entry 16 GiB; expansion ratio 64,000x; chunks 4,000,000; path depth 1,024; metadata 1 GiB; KDF cost 0) and bootstrap_decode_policy (window 8 MiB; working set 384 MiB), documented as deliberately generous for the experimental CLI.
research_needed: Measure realistic archive populations and adversarial decompression-bomb cost to justify each numeric limit.
decision_needed: What default resource limits should the v1 CLI enforce?

statement: CLI sequential reads use bootstrap_sequential_limits: max item 4 GiB, max container 256 GiB, staging memory 256 MiB, total staging 64 GiB, content policy Verify by default.
research_needed: Measure staging spill behaviour and memory bound under large STREAM archives.
decision_needed: Are the STREAM staging/item/container limits appropriate v1 defaults?

statement: No CLI command exposes options to narrow or widen resource budget, decode, staging, or random-access limits; every command uses the bootstrap/default policies.
research_needed: Threat model for untrusted archives in server contexts needing tighter limits.
decision_needed: Should the CLI expose --limit style options or a policy file?

statement: The bootstrap resource policy sets max_key_derivation_cost to 0 while CLI password-only archives use Argon2id; how this caller budget interacts with encrypted/password decoding via the CLI is not established in the CLI slice.
research_needed: Trace KDF cost enforcement for password archives opened via CLI (read/list/inspect/verify).
decision_needed: What maximum Argon2id cost should a default reader accept?

statement: pack takes 1-2 positionals (input directory, optional output or '-') and 7 options: --layout, --stream-window, --profile, --recipient (repeatable), --password, --pad, --chunk-boundary, plus --help/-h as sole argument; all but --recipient are single-use.
When pack output is omitted, the path is default_pack_output(input) from the library.
pack default layout: a regular file output defaults to INDEXED; an output of '-' defaults to STREAM; both use the .eb extension.
--stream-window with a non-STREAM layout is a usage error.

STREAM window default is 0, refusing any cross-object historical dependency; 'auto' declares exactly the minimum the organisation needs; packing fails with a typed diagnostic rather than silently raising a requested window.
evidence_in_source: PACK_HELP; code L595-607, L765; StreamWindow default Ceiling(0) at ecf/stream.rs:206-210; test a_window_that_cannot_be_met_fails_with_a_typed_diagnostic (cli_workflow.rs:277-319)

statement: With the default window 0, packing two files sharing a >3 MiB prefix to STREAM fails with EB_ECF_STREAM_WINDOW_EXCEEDED ('automatic window' hint), so ordinary redundant trees can fail STREAM packing unless the user passes --stream-window auto.
evidence_in_source: integration test demonstrates refusal; no output file left behind
research_needed: Measure how often real corpora exceed window 0 under balanced/dense; usability study of the failure.
decision_needed: Should the STREAM default window be 0, auto, or a bounded non-zero value?

statement: Shared dictionaries are declared before use and do not consume the STREAM window; historical exact-Chunk references and bounded-lookback ChunkGroups may require a non-zero window.
research_needed: Quantify window requirements produced by dense/extreme ChunkGroups.

statement: pack help asserts unencrypted output is deterministic while encrypted output uses fresh secure randomness.
evidence_in_source: help text; publish test compares artifact bytes across target order (lib.rs:5755-5762)
research_needed: Cross-platform, cross-thread-count, cross-build reproducibility tests of pack output bytes.

statement: Profiles are creation-time policy only; archives record their TransformPlans.
JPEG reconstruction is opportunistic, bounded, and committed only after an exact byte round trip.
research_needed: Measure JPEG corpus coverage, fallback rate and net savings.

statement: pack refuses mixing --password with --recipient: PolicyRefused EB_CRYPTO_RECIPIENT_POLICY_INVALID.
decision_needed: Will mixed password+hybrid recipient archives ever be permitted?

statement: --pad and --chunk-boundary without --recipient or --password are a usage error.

Encrypted pack is refused (Unsupported EB_CRYPTO_LAYOUT_UNSUPPORTED) for --layout stream or any stdout destination, even with --layout indexed; checked before input/recipient files are read so no bytes are emitted.
decision_needed: Should encrypted INDEXED output to stdout be supported by buffering?

statement: Encrypted padding defaults to bucketed; --pad none is a recorded privacy-reducing opt-out; --pad max uses the maximum class. Encrypted chunk-boundary default is a secret AFK-derived Gear table; --chunk-boundary keyed-prf selects PHTE/AES-128.
evidence_in_source: PACK_HELP; code L619-645, L726-727; defaults PaddingMode::Bucketed (crypto/mod.rs:74-81), BoundaryMode::SecretGearTable (crypto/mod.rs:100-106)
research_needed: Leakage/efficiency comparison of bucketed vs max padding and secret-Gear vs PHTE boundaries.
decision_needed: Are bucketed padding and secret-Gear boundaries the right v1 defaults?

statement: --recipient may be repeated for X-Wing recipients; --password creates one password-only archive and prompts twice on the controlling terminal.
pack --password only checks that the two prompted passwords match; unlike key change-password (L2825) it does not reject an empty password at the CLI layer.
research_needed: Check whether the library refuses empty passwords during pack_directory_encrypted.
decision_needed: Should empty or weak passwords be refused at creation?

statement: Passwords are only read interactively from the controlling terminal via rpassword; there is no non-interactive source (env var, file, fd), and without a terminal the command fails with PolicyRefused EB_IO.
research_needed: Usability/security trade-off study for CI/automation password input.
decision_needed: Will the CLI support a non-interactive password source?

statement: Encrypted pack builds the whole encrypted archive in memory via pack_directory_encrypted (include_index from PackOptions, no embedded signatures), writes it with exclusive create, removes the file on write failure, and reports entries, padding, boundary, identities and planner.
research_needed: Peak memory of encrypted pack for large trees.

statement: Unencrypted planning (plan_directory) completes before any output object is created, so a plan unrepresentable under requested constraints never leaves a partial archive.
evidence_in_source: code comment; cli_workflow.rs:299-302 asserts no output after refused STREAM window

statement: STREAM pack encodes via encode_stream to stdout or an exclusively created file, removes the file on encode/flush failure, and reports layout STREAM, stream dedup window, budget declared, chunk frames and manifest records.
INDEXED pack encodes the whole archive into memory (ecf::encode) and on a write_all failure to a file does not remove the partially written output, unlike the STREAM and encrypted paths.
research_needed: Fault-injection test (disk full) for pack INDEXED output.
decision_needed: Should INDEXED pack remove partial output on failure and write via temp+rename?

statement: All CLI output files are created with create_new (exclusive); existing destinations are never overwritten and there is no --force/overwrite option.
evidence_in_source: code; unit test deterministic_zip_tar_export_receipt_dry_run_and_reimport_workflow asserts second export fails EB_IO with original bytes unchanged (lib.rs:5660-5675)
decision_needed: Is 'never overwrite, no --force' the frozen CLI policy?

statement: pack exposes no options for chunking parameters, dictionary enablement, thread count, include/exclude filters, metadata capture policy (ownership/xattrs/ACLs), symlink following, source_retries (default 2), omitting the Index (include_index default true), or resource limits.
evidence_in_source: absence in parser; PackOptions default at archive/filesystem.rs:56-64
research_needed: Survey incumbent pack options users rely on (exclude, one-file-system, numeric-owner).
decision_needed: Which pack-time controls are required for v1?

statement: pack passes PackOptions { profile, ..PackOptions::default() }, i.e. source_retries 2, include_index true (archive/filesystem.rs:56-64).
pack's positional-count usage message still mentions only --layout, --stream-window and --profile, omitting the crypto options.
Creation commands print all four identity roots as 'LAI', 'PCR', 'AUX', 'PCI' lines plus planner id.
convert is bidirectional: any --to, --target-profile or their '=' forms routes to legacy export; otherwise convert imports a legacy artifact into .eb.
research_needed: Usability test of a single bidirectional convert verb.
decision_needed: Keep one bidirectional convert verb or split import/export?

statement: convert import takes exactly 2 positionals and 8 options: --strict, --compat (= or space), --preserve, --dry-run, --from (= or space), --entry-name (= or space), --profile, --layout; each single-use.
Import policy: --strict and --compat are mutually exclusive; --preserve requires --compat; with neither, the mode is Strict; --compat alone is Compatibility; --preserve --compat is Preservation.

--compat must name an exact versioned ZIP compatibility profile; an unversioned id such as 'zip/java' fails with EB_ECF_UNSUPPORTED_REQUIRED_FEATURE. Supported ids: zip/python-zipfile@3.13.5, zip/java-zipfile@21.0.12.1, zip/java-zipinputstream@21.0.12.1, zip/libarchive-bsdtar@3.8.8.
research_needed: Keep runtime observed-outcome matrix current as reference implementations release new versions.
decision_needed: How are compat profiles added/deprecated as runtimes evolve?

statement: --compat and --preserve are defined only for ZIP; an explicit or detected non-ZIP source fails with Unsupported EB_ECF_UNSUPPORTED_REQUIRED_FEATURE.
research_needed: Runtime divergence matrices for tar and 7z readers.
decision_needed: Will compatibility/preservation modes extend to tar/7z in v1?

statement: --entry-name is unavailable for ZIP compatibility/preservation imports (usage error).
--from accepts 11 formats: zip, 7z, tar, gzip, zstd, xz, bzip2, tar.gz, tar.zst, tar.xz, tar.bz2; when absent the library detects the format.
evidence_in_source: help text; LegacySourceFormat parse at legacy/import.rs:73-83
research_needed: Detection accuracy on mislabeled/polyglot inputs.

statement: gzip, Zstandard, XZ and bzip2 are bounded transport layers whose decoded children use the tar adapter; a non-tar compressed stream requires --entry-name and becomes a single-file projection.

Help claims ZIP modes retain independent central, local and descriptor observations; strict 7z validates plain/encoded headers, folder graphs, solid streams and a bounded codec/filter subset; strict tar supports ustar, pax, GNU long-name and base-256 evidence.
evidence_in_source: help text; minimal store fixtures in unit tests (store_zip, store_tar, store_sevenz)
research_needed: Conformance corpus with real-world ZIP/7z/tar variants and adversarial samples.

statement: convert import reads its input only from a file path (read(&input)); '-' is not treated as stdin for import, although output '-' is supported.
decision_needed: Should import accept legacy input from stdin?

statement: convert import has no --stream-window option; STREAM output always uses StreamWriteOptions::default() (window 0), so imports needing cross-object references fail rather than using auto.
decision_needed: Should convert expose --stream-window or default to auto?

statement: convert import cannot produce encrypted output: no --recipient/--password options.
decision_needed: Should legacy import support direct encrypted output?

statement: convert import default layout mirrors pack: file output INDEXED, stdout STREAM.
convert --dry-run still requires the output positional, fully encodes the archive in memory (INDEXED) or into a discarded buffer (STREAM), prints identities, and writes nothing.
convert import reads the entire legacy source into memory before import.
research_needed: Memory profile for multi-GB legacy imports.

statement: convert reports source format, mode, compat-profile, preservation, layer chain, wrapper members, decoded child digest, projection, format statistics, entries observed, conflict counts (omission/refinement/divergence/irreconcilable), resolutions and synthesized ancestors.
Preservation mode records exact source plus observations; the unit test recovers the exact ZIP source bytes via recover_preserved_source.
Converted INDEXED output to a file is exclusively created and removed on write failure; STREAM file output is removed on encode failure.
Legacy import uses LegacyImportPolicy::default() and ZipImportPolicy::default(); the CLI offers no options to tune legacy import resource limits.
decision_needed: Should legacy import limits be user-configurable?

statement: convert export takes exactly 2 positionals (archive or '-', target path or '-') and 7 options: --to (= form), --target-profile (= form), --dry-run, --allow-lossy, --receipt, --identity, --password; each single-use.
Export targets are zip, tar, tar.gz, tar.zst, tar.xz, tar.bz2 (six), mapping to profiles such as zip/portable-v1, tar/pax-v1, tar.gz/pax-v1 and tar.zst/pax-v1.
evidence_in_source: help text; ExportTarget parse legacy/export.rs:136-141; tests assert zip/portable-v1, tar.zst/pax-v1, tar.gz/pax-v1

statement: Legacy export offers no 7z, standalone gzip/zstd/xz/bzip2 single-file, cpio, or other targets; only the ZIP and tar family.
research_needed: Gatekeeper analysis of which legacy targets downstream consumers require.
decision_needed: Which additional export targets are needed for dual publishing?

statement: Export requires --to or --target-profile; if both are given they must select the same target (usage error otherwise).
--receipt is unavailable with --dry-run, unsupported when the target is stdout (output cannot be rolled back), and must differ from the target path.

Export authenticates and verifies the source EAM, then completes a typed LOSSLESS/LOSSY/REFUSED preflight before creating output; LOSSY output requires --allow-lossy (EB_LEGACY_EXPORT_LOSSY_APPROVAL_REQUIRED).
evidence_in_source: help text; code L987-1001; unit test deterministic_zip_tar_export_receipt_dry_run_and_reimport_workflow (lib.rs:5606-5706)

statement: Exporting a freshly packed directory containing one regular file to --to=zip without --allow-lossy is refused as LOSSY (EB_LEGACY_EXPORT_LOSSY_APPROVAL_REQUIRED) and leaves no output.
research_needed: Identify which captured metadata makes trivial trees LOSSY for zip/tar and how often real exports need --allow-lossy.
decision_needed: Should common metadata losses (e.g. timestamps precision, ownership) require explicit approval?

statement: zip/portable-v1, tar/pax-v1 and the deterministic compressed-tar profiles are strict-reimported before publication.
evidence_in_source: help text; test re-imports zip/tar targets with --strict and verifies (lib.rs:5677-5691)
research_needed: Confirm reimport check for every target including tar.xz/tar.bz2; cross-reader compatibility of exported bytes.

statement: Compressed-tar export profiles are described as deterministic; byte stability depends on pinned compressor crate behaviour.
research_needed: Byte-stability regression tests across compressor crate upgrades and platforms.
decision_needed: How are deterministic export profiles versioned when compressor output changes?

statement: Export prints entries, target profile, target byte length and target SHA-256; the receipt is canonical JSON containing the target hash and "deterministic":true.

Exporting an encrypted source requires --identity or --password; embedded signatures are verified (no timestamp policy) and counted valid/invalid/stale into ExportSourceSecurity; supplying unlock material for an unencrypted archive is a usage error.

Exporting an authenticated encrypted source to an unencrypted legacy target only prints a warning; no explicit consent flag is required for the plaintext transition (receipt records encrypted:true, target_encrypted:false).
research_needed: Threat-model review of accidental plaintext export.
decision_needed: Should decrypting export require an explicit flag such as --allow-plaintext?

statement: Export of an encrypted archive yields bytes identical to exporting a plain archive of the same input (zip and tar.gz), so legacy output is independent of source encryption.
Embedded-signature verification during export passes no TimestampPolicy, so RFC 3161 timestamps are not evaluated in the export security summary.

Export writes the target directly at its final name (create_new, sync) rather than temp+link; if receipt creation fails both files are removed, but a crash mid-write leaves a partial target visible under the final name.
research_needed: Crash-consistency test for export versus publish's temp+hard-link transaction.
decision_needed: Should single-target export reuse the publish transaction mechanism?

statement: Export reads the full source (path or stdin) into memory; STREAM sources are opened with Retain content policy.
Export --dry-run prints the full analysis; a REFUSED outcome still fails via accept(), other outcomes succeed without writing target bytes.
Export analysis output lists target profile, outcome, entries, logical bytes, planned target bytes, and each issue's category, disposition, entry (or 'archive') and reason.

publish takes exactly one positional (.eb or directory) and 11 options: --output-dir, --native, --target (repeatable, = form), --base-name (= form), --allow-lossy, --dry-run, --report, --identity, --password, --layout, --profile.
publish requires --output-dir naming an existing directory, at least one of --native or --target, forbids identity+password together, and refuses standard input.
publish base name defaults to the directory name or file stem (fallback 'release') and must be non-empty, not '.'/'..', and contain no '/', '\\', ':' or NUL.
Directory sources are planned with --profile (default balanced) and native identities applied; --identity/--password are refused for directories and --profile/--layout are refused for .eb sources.
publish cannot create an encrypted native artifact from a directory (no --recipient option); encrypted native output is only possible by publishing an existing encrypted .eb.
decision_needed: Should publish support encrypted native creation?

statement: Native artifact relation is recorded as 'encoded-from-same-source-eam' (directory, layout default INDEXED, LAI re-verified), 'verified-source-in-place' (output equals source), or 'exact-verified-source-copy' (.eb copied byte-for-byte).
evidence_in_source: code; verify_native_bytes L1515-1542 (LAI mismatch -> Corrupt EB_INTEGRITY_LAI_MISMATCH)

statement: publish encodes a STREAM native artifact with StreamWriteOptions::default() (window 0) and has no --stream-window option, so directory sources needing cross-object references cannot be published as STREAM.

publish verifies/plans the source once; every target is fully analysed, encoded and strict-reimported before any final name is published; temporaries are removed and new names rolled back on failure; target order does not affect artifact or report bytes.

transactional_publish writes each artifact to an exclusive temp sibling '.<name>.entrybound-tmp-<pid>-<ordinal>-<attempt>' (up to 1024 attempts), syncs, then hard-links each to its final name, rolling back published names and temps on any failure.
evidence_in_source: code; unit test asserts rollback when a later parent is missing (lib.rs:5788-5800)

statement: Publication (and repack staging, L3516) relies on std::fs::hard_link; filesystems without hard-link support (e.g. FAT/exFAT, some network or cloud-synced filesystems) would make publish/repack fail.
research_needed: Test publish/repack on exFAT, SMB, NFS, and cloud-sync folders on Windows/macOS/Linux.
decision_needed: Is a rename-based fallback needed where hard links are unavailable?

statement: Collision checks (path.exists) run before commit, leaving a TOCTOU window mitigated by exclusive hard_link; a process crash mid-transaction leaves temp siblings and possibly some final names without automatic recovery.
research_needed: Crash-injection testing of publish between link steps.
decision_needed: Is crash-leftover cleanup/recovery required?

statement: Transaction path validation rejects duplicate outputs (usage), existing destinations (PolicyRefused EB_EXTRACT_COLLISION) and missing parent directories.
evidence_in_source: code; unit test blocked directory case (lib.rs:5764-5786) leaves pre-existing file intact and creates nothing

statement: publish --dry-run prints the canonical migration report JSON and fails if not ready: LOSSY -> PolicyRefused EB_LEGACY_EXPORT_LOSSY_APPROVAL_REQUIRED, REFUSED -> Unsupported EB_LEGACY_EXPORT_REFUSED, otherwise Nonconforming EB_LEGACY_EXPORT_TARGET_INVALID.

Migration report uses format id 'entrybound/migration-report-v1', records overall_publish_outcome PUBLISHED, and orders targets canonically (tar.zst/pax-v1 before zip/portable-v1) regardless of CLI order.
Migration and sidecar reports embed output paths rendered from the caller-supplied directory (display strings), so report bytes depend on local paths and platform path syntax.
research_needed: Check report reproducibility across machines/OS path separators.
decision_needed: Should reports record relative artifact names instead of absolute/display paths?

statement: publish warns that legacy targets are unencrypted while the native .eb retains Entrybound crypto/signature state.
publish holds the source bytes and every prepared artifact in memory before committing.
research_needed: Memory ceiling for multi-target publish of large trees.

statement: sidecar takes 1-2 positionals and 8 options: --strict, --preserve, --compat (= or space), --from (= or space), --entry-name, --layout, --profile (= or space), --report.

sidecar default output is '<legacy-artifact>.eb'; the source is never modified; the sidecar is reopened and verified, including ConversionProvenance binding to the exact source SHA-256, before its final name is published.
evidence_in_source: help text; code L1818-1896; unit test sidecar_binds_exact_legacy_source_and_verifies_before_publish (lib.rs:5804-5897)

statement: sidecar refuses '-' as source and refuses an output path equal to the source.
read_stable_source compares file length and modification time before and after reading; any change fails with PolicyRefused EB_INPUT_SOURCE_UNSTABLE.

Source-stability detection uses only length and mtime; a same-length rewrite within mtime granularity (or with preserved mtime) is not detected, so the SHA-256 bound may describe bytes that differ from the file afterwards.
research_needed: Measure mtime granularity per filesystem (FAT 2 s, ext4 ns) and evaluate change-detection gaps.
decision_needed: Is length+mtime sufficient, or should sidecar re-hash or lock the source?

statement: Sidecar migration report records source_kind 'legacy-sidecar', relation 'native-sidecar-of-exact-legacy-source', conflict_count (sum of four conflict classes), resolution_count, exact_source_preserved, verification_succeeded true.
Running sidecar twice for the same source fails with EB_EXTRACT_COLLISION and leaves the source unchanged.
sidecar layout defaults to INDEXED; tests cover tar.zst sidecars as STREAM and 7z sidecars as INDEXED.
sidecar compatibility and preservation modes accept only versioned ZIP profiles.
sidecar has no --dry-run, no encryption options, and always writes status to stdout.

unpack takes 1-2 positionals and 10 options: --symlinks refuse|safe|all, --restore-owner, --xattrs ignore|restore, --sparse logical|restore, --acls ignore|restore, --windows-security ignore|restore, --reparse refuse|known-safe|all, --platform-metadata ignore|restore, --identity, --password.

CLI unpack starts from ExtractionPolicy::default: collision Refuse, symlinks Safe, ownership Ignore, xattrs Ignore, sparse Logical, ACLs Ignore, Windows security Ignore, reparse Refuse, platform metadata Ignore, bootstrap resource and decode policies.
research_needed: Security review of 'safe' symlink semantics; usability of default metadata non-restoration versus tar -p expectations.
decision_needed: Are these conservative extraction defaults frozen for v1?

statement: unpack metadata policy options may be repeated with last value winning (no duplicate check), unlike most other CLI options which reject repeats.
unpack has no option to choose collision handling (CollisionPolicy only has Refuse), no entry selection/filter, no strip-components, and no explicit opposite of --restore-owner.
research_needed: Survey of extraction workflows needing merge/overwrite/subset extraction.
decision_needed: Which extraction selection and collision options are required for v1?

statement: unpack default destination is default_unpack_destination(archive path); unpacking from stdin requires an explicit destination.

For stdin sources, commands infer encryption from whether unlock material was supplied; an encrypted archive piped without --identity/--password is routed to the unencrypted STREAM reader, so the user-facing diagnostic is not the crypto one.
research_needed: Test diagnostics for encrypted archive piped without unlock.
decision_needed: Should stdin input be sniffed (buffer preamble) to detect encryption?

statement: Encrypted unpack reads the whole archive into memory, fully authenticates and verifies via open_encrypted before any extraction, and reports 'authenticated, verified, and unpacked'; a tampered ciphertext creates no destination.
Supplying --identity/--password for an unencrypted archive is a usage error (same rule in inspect, verify, explain, sign, export).

STREAM unpack (stdin or file declaring STREAM) uses unpack_stream with bootstrap sequential limits, reports staging peak-resident-bytes, spilled-bytes and peak-retained-chunks, and states destination objects were created only after the complete archive verified.
research_needed: Measure staging spill and peak memory for large STREAM archives.

statement: Unencrypted INDEXED unpack reads the entire archive file into memory before extraction.
research_needed: RSS measurement for multi-GB INDEXED unpack.
decision_needed: Must INDEXED unpack avoid whole-file reads for v1 scalability?

statement: unpack reports confinement as 'kernel-enforced capability-relative' or 'weaker platform mode (reported)'.
research_needed: Enumerate which OS/filesystem combinations yield KernelEnforced vs WeakerReported.
decision_needed: Should weaker confinement require opt-in rather than being only reported?

statement: unpack prints metadata limitations from ExtractionReport.metadata_not_restored, or states all represented and platform-supported items were restored.
unpack, verify, explain accept only local paths or '-', not HTTP(S) URLs; remote access is limited to read, list, inspect and diff.
decision_needed: Is remote verify/unpack in scope for v1?

statement: read takes 2 positionals (archive path or URL, logical path) and 4 options: --output <file|->, --access-report, --identity, --password.
Random-access sources are a local file (LocalFileRandomReadSource) or an http:// or https:// URL (HttpRangeSource); '-' is refused with Unsupported EB_RANDOM_ACCESS_NOT_INDEXED.
Plain http:// URLs are accepted for range-backed access, not only https://.
research_needed: Threat analysis: integrity is verified cryptographically but metadata/privacy of access patterns over cleartext HTTP.
decision_needed: Should cleartext http:// sources be refused or require an opt-in flag?

statement: CLI logical paths are UTF-8 strings split on '/' into LogicalPath::from_utf8 components; non-UTF-8 input is a usage error.

CLI random access always uses RandomAccessPolicy::default: 64 MiB per range, 512 MiB total fetched, 100,000 requests, 128 MiB metadata, 64 sections, 4,000,000 chunk frames scanned, 65,536 dependency chunks, 8 GiB decoded, 128 MiB cache, 4,000,000 segment-header walk, 100,000 trace entries, 4,096-byte coalesce gap.
research_needed: HTTP range benchmarks (latency, request count, coalescing) to justify defaults.
decision_needed: Are these remote-access defaults appropriate for v1?

statement: read materialises only the requested verified entry; status states 'requested entry VERIFIED ... whole archive verified: false'; output defaults to stdout (status then to stderr), file output is exclusive and removed on failure.
evidence_in_source: code; unit test read_command_materializes_only_a_verified_indexed_entry (lib.rs:6012-6083) for plain and encrypted archives

statement: --access-report prints verification scope, source revision stability, index status, verified and dependency chunk counts, LAI/AUX/PCR/PCI statuses, range count, transferred bytes, and every range with offset, length, purpose and cache hit/miss.
read works only on INDEXED archives (encrypted or not); STREAM archives cannot be read by path because the random-access reader refuses STREAM (ecf/container.rs:837-841).
decision_needed: Should read fall back to a sequential scan for STREAM archives?

statement: read buffers the whole entry in memory (result.bytes) before writing; no streaming output for large entries; one entry per invocation and no metadata restoration.
research_needed: Memory profile of read for multi-GB entries (bounded by 8 GiB decoded default).

statement: No CLI test exercises HTTP(S) range sources for read, list, inspect or diff; HTTP access is untested at the CLI layer.
research_needed: Add a local HTTP range server fixture test for CLI remote commands.

statement: list takes one positional (path, URL or '-') and 2 options: --identity, --password.

list uses range-backed random access when the source is a URL or unlock material is given, printing to stderr that only the metadata view was authenticated/hashed and the whole archive was not verified, with ranges, bytes and index status.
list of a local unencrypted archive fully verifies it (StreamContentPolicy::Verify) and for STREAM notes the listing required a complete sequential pass.
Listing an encrypted archive from stdin is impossible: unlock material forces the random-access path, which refuses '-'.
list of a local encrypted archive without unlock takes the unencrypted load/open path rather than printing public framing like inspect; the resulting diagnostic is not established by the CLI.
research_needed: Test list on encrypted archive without unlock.

statement: list output is one line per entry 'kind<TAB>path' with kinds directory, file, symlink, reparse-point; no sizes, metadata, or JSON mode.
decision_needed: Does list need --json or long format for v1 tooling?

statement: repack takes 2 positionals and 5 options: --layout, --profile, --index preserve|present|absent, --stream-window <n>|auto, --dry-run; repeats are not rejected (last wins).

repack without --profile is representation-only: recorded Chunk boundaries, plans, dictionaries, groups, reconstruction and physical order are retained and LAI/AUX/PCR must remain equal; with --profile it performs a current-v6 replan requiring LAI/AUX equality.
evidence_in_source: help text; code L3395-3403; unit test repack_diff_structured_inspect_and_entry_explain_workflow (lib.rs:6085-6178)

statement: Encrypted repack is refused with Unsupported EB_CRYPTO_LAYOUT_UNSUPPORTED: it 'requires a future crypto-aware mutation contract'.
research_needed: Design crypto-aware repack semantics (AFK reuse, signature staleness, padding).
decision_needed: Will encrypted repack be defined before v1?

statement: repack defaults: target layout = source layout, --index preserve, STREAM window Auto; the Auto default differs from pack/convert/publish whose STREAM window default is 0.
decision_needed: Should STREAM window defaults be unified across commands?

statement: repack refuses --stream-window for non-STREAM output and --index present/absent for STREAM output ('STREAM has no Index').
repack loads its source from a path only (no stdin or URL) with StreamContentPolicy::Retain.

repack prints a PROSPECTIVE or VERIFIED comparison: mode, layout and planner transitions, logical/unique chunk counts, stored bytes, working set, dictionaries/groups/regions, LAI/AUX/PCR equality, prospective container bytes, source/target PCR.

repack output is staged to a temp sibling, synced, re-read and fully verified (INDEXED open or STREAM Verify), then hard-linked exclusively to the final name; an existing output is refused (PolicyRefused EB_IO).
repack reports 'exact no-op repack: PCI and bytes reproduced' when representation-only output equals source bytes, else 'semantic/physical equivalent; container rewritten'.
research_needed: Corpus test that representation-only repack of canonical archives is byte-identical.

statement: Replan is tied to 'current-v6' planner; behaviour for archives from older planners or when a v7 planner appears is not specified in the CLI.
decision_needed: How does repack select planner versions as the planner evolves?

statement: diff takes 2 positionals and 6 options: --json, --public, --left-identity, --right-identity, --left-password, --right-password.

diff reports SEMANTIC (LAI), AUXILIARY (AUX), PHYSICAL (PCR) and CONTAINER/PCI changes separately; URL inputs use verified range-backed metadata and report PCR NOT_VERIFIED and PCI NOT_COMPUTED unless fully read.

diff --public compares only public encrypted framing (required_features, payload_suite, recipient_count, recipient_types, padding, boundary, segment_count, total_container_bytes) as Container-tier changes; LAI/AUX/PCR NOT_VERIFIED, PCI NOT_COMPUTED; unlock material is refused.
Local full diff appends Container-tier 'security' changes for encrypted flag, payload suite, recipient_set_digest, archive_id, embedded signature count and stale signature count.

diff text output shows identity statuses, interpretation, per-side verification scope, physical summary (chunks reused/added/removed, boundary-changed objects) and per-change tier/subject/field/left/right; --json emits canonical JSON.
diff loads identity files without the Unix permission warning used elsewhere, and '-' is treated as a file path (no stdin).

inspect takes one positional (path, URL or '-') and 12 options: --json, --entries, --plans, --chunks, --reconstruction, --provenance, --security, --access, --crypto, --identity, --password, --timestamp-trust (repeatable).
Help presents --entries|--plans|--chunks and --reconstruction|--provenance|--security|--access as alternatives, but the parser accepts any combination of focused views.

Default inspect of a local unencrypted archive fully verifies it and prints format, version, layout, archive role, entry count, logical bytes, feature bits, feature presence, stream window, budget declaration, random lookup, planner, chunker, chunk/cross-file/group/reconstruction statistics, plans, codec/transform usage, identities, index, stream stats, fidelity, conversion, preservation, declared resources and decode requirements.
inspect's archive-role match has a single arm, Complete; partial/incremental archive roles do not exist in the CLI.
decision_needed: Are incremental/partial roles deferred beyond v1?

statement: When a producer did not declare a budget, inspect states caller policy alone bounded decoding and absence is not a claim of unlimited resources.
evidence_in_source: code text; stream test asserts 'declared before the payload' (cli_workflow.rs:202)

statement: inspect states random entry lookup is unavailable for STREAM, requiring a complete sequential scan or a repack.

Encrypted inspect without unlock prints only public framing (payload suite, recipient count, stanza types, padding, boundary, segment count, container bytes), warns when padding is None, and states private metadata is locked.
evidence_in_source: code; test crypto_cli.rs:55-60 asserts no private path leaks
research_needed: Evaluate what public framing reveals (recipient count/types, segment count).

statement: Authenticated encrypted inspect reports encrypted Descriptor record version 2 when FEATURE_PRIVATE_RESOURCE_DECLARATION_V1 is set (declared resources and decode validated against archive reality) else 1, plus embedded signature statuses using --timestamp-trust anchors.
evidence_in_source: code; test crypto_cli.rs:62-79 asserts version 2 and 'matches authenticated archive reality'

statement: Encrypted archives lacking the producer resource declaration are still accepted and labelled 'legacy experimental crypto-v1'.
decision_needed: When will legacy experimental crypto-v1 archives without resource declarations stop being accepted?

statement: inspect of an HTTP(S) URL gives a range-backed metadata view: with --crypto and no unlock only public framing (PCR not fetched, PCI NOT_COMPUTED); otherwise encrypted flag, source revision, container bytes, entries, planner, chunker, LAI/AUX/PCR with statuses, PCI status, index, physical directory records; whole_archive_verified false.
Focused inspect views are ignored for URL sources (non-JSON), and --timestamp-trust is ignored by --json and URL inspection paths.

inspect --json emits library canonical JSON (inspection_json, inspection_json_with_security, random_inspection_json); for locked encrypted archives it emits a hand-formatted 'entrybound/inspection-v1' document with public fields and null identities.
research_needed: Schema stability/versioning tests for inspection JSON.
decision_needed: Is entrybound/inspection-v1 a stable machine interface?

statement: Authenticated encrypted inspect JSON hard-codes payload_suite as 'payload-suite-v1' instead of deriving it from the archive's addressing payload_suite_id.
decision_needed: Should the JSON report the actual suite id?

statement: Focused text views print 'inspection scope: whole archive verified' and selected facts; --security prints encrypted flag and 'secret material exposed: false'; --access prints layout, random lookup, index, window and lookback cost.

inspect prints fidelity captured/unavailable classes, conversion provenance (adapter, mode, digest, outcome, conflict counts, up to 16 resolutions, layer chain) and preservation evidence (format, source bytes/digest, observations, conflicts, opaque count, exact-source-recovery=yes).

Index status strings: present and valid; absent rebuilt from authoritative CHUNK_DATA; invalid rebuilt from authoritative CHUNK_DATA; not applicable for STREAM by design, reflecting that the Index is a rebuildable cache.
explain takes 1-2 positionals (archive or '-', optional logical path) and 2 options: --identity, --password.
explain labels every fact with an evidence class: RECORDED, DERIVED, AUDIT, NOT_RECORDED.
evidence_in_source: code; unit test runs entry explain (lib.rs:6164-6170)

statement: explain re-derives planner alternatives, so STREAM sources are scanned with a Retain content policy and a note says a complete sequential pass was required; encrypted explain requires unlock and has no URL support.

Aggregate explain prints planner, logical/plaintext/stored bytes, unique chunks and references, exact dedup savings and ratio, chunk sizes, STORE and Zstandard stats, total savings, replayed NOT_RECORDED estimates (codec, dictionary, lookback, reconstructive, structural), AUDIT fallbacks, DERIVED JPEG savings and similarity cohorts.
explain breaks down only STORE and Zstandard codec usage, while help advertises LZ4 and LZMA2 planning (L122-123); LZ4/LZMA2 contributions are not itemised in the aggregate explanation.
decision_needed: Should explain itemise every codec in the registry?

statement: Savings for independent codecs, shared dictionaries, bounded lookback and reconstruction are replayed comparison estimates marked NOT_RECORDED, not measurements stored in the archive.
research_needed: Validate replay estimates against actual alternative encodings on a corpus.

statement: verify takes one positional and 9 options: --signatures, --signature (repeatable), --timestamp-trust (repeatable), --require-signature, --require-content-signature, --require-physical-signature, --require-addressing-signature, --identity, --password.
Global help documents only --signatures|--signature and unlock for verify; --timestamp-trust and the four --require-*-signature options are undocumented.
decision_needed: Document or rename the signature policy options?

statement: Unencrypted verify claims canonical structure, section integrity, semantic invariants, Dictionary/ChunkGroup/ReconstructionData dependencies and access costs, reconstructed Chunk bytes, content integrity, Entry identities, LAI, PCR, AUX and exact-byte PCI; STREAM adds item framing/order, stored lengths, window constraints, footer binding and exact length.
research_needed: Mutation/fuzz corpus proving each claimed check detects corruption.

statement: verify of an encrypted archive without unlock validates only public framing, prints 'PRIVATE CONTENT UNVERIFIED', and exits 0 (success).
research_needed: Usability study: do scripts misinterpret exit 0 as full verification?
decision_needed: Should unverified private content yield a non-zero or distinct exit status?

statement: Requesting signature evaluation or a non-default signature policy on an encrypted archive without unlock is a usage error.

Authenticated encrypted verify checks CryptoEnvelope commitment/MAC, every AEAD DATA/END record, segment order/finality, canonical private ECF, semantic invariants, content integrity, LAI, PCR, AUX, exact-byte PCI, then enforces signature policy.
Embedded signatures (--signatures) on unencrypted archives are refused: Unsupported EB_SIGNATURE_UNSUPPORTED, 'unencrypted ECF has no normative embedded-signature placement; supply .ebsig'.
decision_needed: Will unencrypted ECF gain a normative embedded-signature placement?

statement: Detached .ebsig signatures are read and verified against current bindings for encrypted and unencrypted (INDEXED and STREAM) archives, and SignaturePolicy.enforce applies --require-* flags (all false by default, crypto/signature.rs:315-321).
RFC 3161 timestamp verification time is the local system clock (SystemTime::now) with DER trust anchors from files; a manipulated or skewed clock changes timestamp validity outcomes.
research_needed: Threat model for local clock trust in offline timestamp validation.
decision_needed: Should verify accept an explicit --at-time or reference time?

statement: Signature status lines report signer id, binding mask, cryptographic VALID/INVALID/UNSUPPORTED, content/physical/addressing VALID/STALE/NOT_BOUND, timestamp VALID/INVALID/UNSUPPORTED/ABSENT and optional time.

sign takes one positional and 8 options: --signing-key (required), --detached [file], --embed, --identity, --password, --bind-physical, --bind-addressing, --timestamp-token; --embed and --detached are mutually exclusive.
Frozen CLI policy: sign every binding the archive can provide, CONTENT+PHYSICAL for plaintext plus ADDRESSING after encrypted unlock; CONTENT is always bound and PHYSICAL binds PCR, not PCI.

--bind-physical is a no-op because bind_physical is initialised true; the CLI cannot create content-only signatures that would survive physical repacks. --bind-addressing on plaintext reaches sign_archive, which refuses (EB_SIGNATURE_STALE_ADDRESSING path, crypto/signature.rs:372-379).
research_needed: Assess demand for content-only signatures across repack/re-layout.
decision_needed: Should the CLI offer an option to omit the PHYSICAL binding?

statement: --embed on an unencrypted archive is refused: Unsupported EB_SIGNATURE_UNSUPPORTED ('embedded signatures are defined only for encrypted INDEXED crypto-v1; use .ebsig').
sign opens unencrypted archives with the INDEXED reader (ecf::open) only, so STREAM archives cannot be signed via the CLI even though detached verification of STREAM archives works.
decision_needed: Should sign support STREAM archives?

statement: Embedded signing rewrites encrypted private CONTROL data without rotating the AFK or rewriting bulk payload ciphertext and atomically replaces the archive; detached signing writes one canonical type-26 record to '<archive>.ebsig' by default (exclusive create, sync).

--detached takes the following token as its path only if it does not start with '--' and the archive positional was already seen; otherwise the default path is used, so argument order changes meaning.
decision_needed: Should --detached use an explicit --output path instead?

statement: RFC 3161 timestamp tokens are supplied externally via --timestamp-token; Entrybound never contacts a TSA.
sign does not reject repeated --signing-key, --identity, --password or --embed (last wins/idempotent); identity+password together is rejected in load_unlock (L2896-2903).
key has 5 subcommands: generate-signing, list, add, remove, change-password; key --help prints KEY_HELP.
key generate-signing creates an Ed25519 signing key with exclusive create and sync, then restricts permissions to 0600 on Unix; on non-Unix the restriction is a no-op (L2981-2984).
research_needed: Windows ACL hardening options for secret key files.
decision_needed: Must the CLI restrict secret-key ACLs on Windows?

statement: There is no CLI command to generate X-Wing identity/recipient key pairs; tests create them via the library XWingIdentity::generate, so CLI-only users cannot create hybrid recipients.
evidence_in_source: absence in key dispatch; crypto_cli.rs:38-40 uses library
decision_needed: Add 'key generate-identity' (and recipient export) for v1?

statement: Identity and signing-key files trigger a warning when group/other readable only on Unix; on other platforms no permission check occurs.
key list requires unlock and prints protection PASSWORD_ONLY (one password stanza, no public-key directory) or HYBRID_ONLY with each stanza id, type, class HYBRID_PQ, fingerprint and label.
evidence_in_source: code; test crypto_cli.rs:211-225 (two fingerprints after add)

statement: key add requires exactly one --recipient and --identity (password unlock not accepted); it rewraps the existing AFK, preserves archive ID, and warns addressing signatures may now be stale.
evidence_in_source: code; test crypto_cli.rs:184-209 shows addressing=STALE with content/physical VALID

statement: Recipients cannot be added to password-only archives (key add needs --identity, and password/hybrid mixing is refused).
decision_needed: Should password-to-hybrid migration be supported?

statement: key remove requires every retained public key via --retain and performs fresh-AFK full re-encryption; deleting a stanza is never treated as revocation.
evidence_in_source: code; KEY_HELP L272-274; test crypto_cli.rs:227-260 removed identity fails verify

statement: key change-password requires --password, prompts for current, new and confirmation, rejects empty or mismatched new passwords, and performs fresh-AFK full re-encryption.

Key mutations and embedded signing accept an undocumented --output to write a separate exclusive file; otherwise replace_verified writes a synced temp, renames the original to a backup, renames the temp into place, and removes the backup.
evidence_in_source: code (L2801-2807, L2874-2880); library verifies mutation output (crypto/container.rs verify_mutation_output)

statement: replace_verified is not crash-atomic: between renaming the original to backup and installing the replacement no file exists at the original path; temp/backup names are fixed per PID and a leftover causes failure.
research_needed: Crash-injection test; evaluate platform atomic replace (rename-over, ReplaceFileW).
decision_needed: Should in-place mutation use an atomic replace primitive?

statement: No CLI support for AFK rotation without recipient removal, recipient labels, or hybrid identity rotation.

Shared read-argument parsing accepts --identity and --password once each, rejects them together, rejects unknown '--' options, and loads identities with XWingIdentity::read_file and passwords into Zeroizing strings.
Any argument starting with '--' is treated as an option; there is no '--' end-of-options marker, so paths beginning with '--' cannot be passed.
The CLI uses a hand-written parser; '--opt=value' is accepted only for some options (--to, --target-profile, --target, --base-name, --compat, --from, --entry-name, and --profile only in sidecar).
decision_needed: Adopt a uniform option syntax (e.g. a standard parser) before v1?

statement: The command name and option values must be valid UTF-8; archive and destination paths are carried as OsString and may be non-UTF-8.
Per-command --help/-h (as the sole argument) exists for pack, convert, publish, sidecar, repack, diff, sign and key; unpack, read, list, inspect, verify and explain have none.
No global flags for verbosity, quiet, color, progress reporting, thread count, or config file/environment configuration exist.
decision_needed: Which global UX flags are needed for v1?

statement: No commands exist for append/update/delete of entries, multi-volume archives, mounting, external parity/ECC binding, incremental or base-chained archives.
decision_needed: Which of these are deferred past v1 versus non-goals?

statement: Option complexity per command: pack 7, convert-import 8, convert-export 7, publish 11, sidecar 8, unpack 10, read 4, list 2, repack 5, diff 6, inspect 12, verify 9, sign 8, key generate-signing 0, key list 2, key add 3, key remove 3, key change-password 2, explain 2 (including undocumented --output and --require-* options).
research_needed: Usability testing of option load versus incumbents; identify options to merge or hide.
decision_needed: Is this option surface acceptable for v1 or should it be simplified?

statement: cli_workflow.rs has 9 binary-level tests: all_native_commands_operate_on_real_archives, pack_help_and_profile_option_are_available_only_at_creation, malformed_archive_prints_stable_diagnostic_and_fails, entrybound_alias_uses_the_same_cli_implementation, a_real_pipe_carries_a_stream_archive_from_pack_to_verify, stream_archives_round_trip_through_standard_input_and_output, a_stream_archive_in_a_file_is_never_reported_as_random_access, a_truncated_stream_reports_truncation_rather_than_generic_corruption, a_window_that_cannot_be_met_fails_with_a_typed_diagnostic.

crypto_cli.rs has 2 binary-level tests: hybrid_pack_public_inspect_verify_and_unpack (pack, public/private inspect, verify, unpack, tamper, embed sign, key add/list/remove) and detached_signing_cli_enforces_requested_bindings.

lib.rs has 18 in-process unit tests: unpack_metadata_policies_are_explicit, help_is_available, strict_convert_verify_inspect_and_unpack_workflow, sevenz_convert_supports_indexed_stream_and_dry_run, tar_and_standalone_wrapper_convert_to_indexed_and_stream, compat_preserve_and_dry_run_workflows_are_explicit, preserve_requires_an_exact_compatibility_profile, future_commands_fail_explicitly, stream_window_is_rejected_for_the_indexed_layout, an_unknown_layout_is_a_usage_error, encrypted_stream_is_rejected_before_input_or_output_is_touched, password_and_hybrid_creation_cannot_be_mixed, deterministic_zip_tar_export_receipt_dry_run_and_reimport_workflow, publish_is_canonical_multi_target_and_transactional, sidecar_binds_exact_legacy_source_and_verifies_before_publish, encrypted_export_requires_authentication_and_records_security_transition, read_command_materializes_only_a_verified_indexed_entry, repack_diff_structured_inspect_and_entry_explain_workflow.

CLI tests do not cover: password prompting (pack --password, key change-password), --pad/--chunk-boundary, timestamp tokens and trust anchors, unpack restore options end-to-end, diff --public or encrypted diff, inspect focused text views, key list on password archives, tar.xz/tar.bz2 export, publish --dry-run, convert to stdout, INDEXED via stdin, or fault-injection of transactions.
research_needed: Extend CLI test matrix (pty-based password tests, HTTP range fixture, fault injection).

statement: Unit test repack_diff_structured_inspect_and_entry_explain_workflow covers INDEXED->STREAM repack with auto window, STREAM->INDEXED dense replan with --index absent, dry-run repack, diff --json, inspect --json --plans --chunks, entry explain and verify of the replanned archive.
A STREAM archive truncated by 200 bytes and piped to verify fails with exit 3 and 'TRUNCATED EB_ECF_TRUNCATED_STREAM' rather than generic corruption.
